tells.1: Bolded topic-sentence lead-ins on every rationale point, plus templated 'Mitigation:' labels and the stock closer 'I'm happy to walk through the analysis and take questions.'
tells.2: An overly tidy, symmetrical template: identical section scaffolding, perfectly parallel bullets, and a placeholder financial block that reads like a generated framework.
tells.4: Formulaic 'Mitigation:' labels repeated on every risk, with bolded section headers and perfectly parallel 'X to do Y by [date]' next steps.

reason: Version 3 reads most clearly human: it is rambling and imprecise, with phrases like 'people planning early', but it is too vague and thin to send. Version 2 keeps the complete, credible structure and replaces the canned 'Mitigation:' labels and bold lead-ins with direct first-person commitments, so it reads the most natural of the polished drafts.
